newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close lower in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close lower in active trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Friday due to pre-weekend profit-taking and Wall Street- induced caution on the near term outlook for the local market, brokers said.
"After four days of declines on Wall Street, we had to expect some consolidation of the Hang Seng," said the sales director of Japanese brokerage.
The Hang Seng Index closed 85.18 points down at 12,388.38, off a low of 12,343.27. Turnover remained robust at HK$6.65 billion, down from Thursday's HK$7.12 billion.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 44 points at 5,992 on Thursday, the fourth straight day of declines.
However, brokers were not worried that Wall Street's weakness would shake confidence in the longer term outlook for the market.
"Selling doesn't seem particularly heavy today," said the Japanese broker. "But traders may be looking to hold the index up in advance of the expiry of the October (futures) contract."
The October Hang Seng Index futures contract, which expires on October 30, declined 82 points to 12,380, an eight-point discount to the cash market.
"This is just a retracement of recent gains, providing trading opportunities," said Alice Lee, technical analyst at Tai Fook Securities. "We don't see any selling pressure."
Utilities were the worst performing issues, following by finance. Only the H share sector of China plays bucked the market's downtrend.
In the utility sector, Hong Kong Telecomm dropped HK$0.25 to HK$13.45 on active trade of HK$229.79 million, and China Light lost HK$0.30 to HK$35.80.
Banking giant HSBC ended the day off HK$1.50 at HK$156.50, recovering from a dip to HK$155.50.
Turnover in the share, the most active of the day, totalled HK$557.65 million, about 8.4 percent of total market turnover.
"Since HSBC accounts for more than 15 percent of the market's total capitalisation, this is not really excessive trade in the counter," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.

Henderson Land was the second most active stock and biggest net gainer of the day. The share rose HK$0.75 to close at HK$71.25 after hitting an all time high of HK$71.50. Turnover in the share was HK$366.12 million.
